## `strings.Cut` — signature and semantics

**Exact signature** (as declared in `src/strings/strings.go`, Go 1.18+):

```go
func Cut(s, sep string) (before, after string, found bool)
```

The three names are part of the declared signature, not just the docs.

### Meaning of each return value

`Cut` slices `s` around the **first** instance of `sep`. Doc comment, verbatim:

> `// Cut slices s around the first instance of sep,`
> `// returning the text before and after sep.`
> `// The found result reports whether sep appears in s.`
> `// If sep does not appear in s, cut returns s, "", false.`

| Result | When `sep` **is** present | When `sep` is **not** present |
|---|---|---|
| `before` | the text of `s` preceding the first `sep` = `s[:i]` (may be `""` if `sep` is at the start) | **the whole input `s`** (not `""`) |
| `after` | the text following that first `sep` = `s[i+len(sep):]` (may be `""` if `sep` is at the end) | `""` |
| `found` | `true` | `false` |

So `before + sep + after == s` whenever `found` is true, and the not-found case is exactly `s, "", false`. That last asymmetry is deliberate — the `bool` adds information rather than signalling "no values", which is why `CutPrefix`/`CutSuffix` (Go 1.20) can build on it.

Official example, all four cases:

```
Cut("Gopher", "Go")     = "", "pher", true
Cut("Gopher", "ph")     = "Go", "er", true
Cut("Gopher", "er")     = "Goph", "", true
Cut("Gopher", "Badger") = "Gopher", "", false
```

### Version and idiomatic use

Introduced in **Go 1.18** (2022-03-15) — release notes: *"The new Cut function slices a string around a separator. It can replace and simplify many common uses of Index, IndexByte, IndexRune, and SplitN."*

```go
if before, after, found := strings.Cut(s, "="); found {
	fmt.Println(before, "->", after)
}
```

### One caveat worth knowing

The docs don't spell out the empty separator: since `Index(s, "") == 0`, `Cut(s, "")` returns `"", s, true`, not `found == false`. That follows from the implementation, not the doc text.

   > `configuration.md` › *Models / Agents*
   
   Donc vider les `model_ref` de tous les agents les fait basculer sur le modèle du leader — mais la doc ne le présente pas comme un levier « flotte entière » officiel, seulement comme une règle d'héritage.

   > « `OMNIS_PROVIDER`, `OMNIS_MODEL`, `OMNIS_BASE_URL`, and `OMNIS_API_KEY` override the leader agent model selection. »

   > « Each agent references a model by its profile name via `model_ref` in `registry/agents/<name>/agent.json`. »

> `14-config.md` › *Read root (config search chain)*

Vous avez demandé **comment** faire, pas de le faire — et je n'ai pas de confirmation sur le modèle cible. Je n'ai donc **rien modifié** : réécrire le modèle de 29 agents est une opération large et facile à regretter, pas une étape à franchir sur une hypothèse. Tout reste en l'état.
